narrative:
The model estimated a 54% chance that you would be a bad credit risk, which was high enough for your application to be denied. This does not mean repayment problems are certain; it means the information provided looked somewhat more risky than safe to the model.

The strongest factor was your credit history. Your record shows no credits or all paid, a category seen for only about 1% of approved applicants. That unusual pattern pushed the decision most strongly toward bad risk. Next, your checking-account status of 0–200 DM also increased the risk estimate; approved applicants more often have no balance or a salary-type account, while only about 18% fall in your category. Your real estate ownership worked in your favour and pulled the decision toward good credit, but it was not enough to offset the first two concerns. Other details, such as requesting 1,778 DM over 15 months, were less influential in this decision.

To improve a future application, build a clearer credit record by using credit responsibly and paying on time, keep your checking-account balance healthy, and consider applying for a smaller amount or waiting until your credit history is stronger. You may also ask the lender what specific records they can review or correct.
